title: INDEXED BY vs SUBSCRIPT — INDEX holds a displacement, SUBSCRIPT holds an occurrence number
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. INDEX-VS-SUBSCRIPT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-TABLE.
           05  WS-ROW OCCURS 100 TIMES
                       INDEXED BY WS-IX.
               10  WS-COL  PIC X(10).
       01  WS-SUBSCRIPT    PIC 9(3).
      *> WS-IX is an INDEX -- compile-time-bound to the table.
      *>   Internally a byte displacement. SET WS-IX TO 3 -> points
      *>   to row 3.
      *> WS-SUBSCRIPT is a plain numeric -- WS-ROW(WS-SUBSCRIPT) is
      *>   the same row 3 but goes via runtime multiplication.
      *> SET WS-IX UP BY 1 = increment; you CANNOT do MOVE WS-IX TO
      *>   WS-SUBSCRIPT without conversion.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           STOP RUN.
notes: INDEXED BY behaves like a C/C++ pointer-into-array; plain SUBSCRIPT is a row number. The two cannot be assigned to each other directly. A Java rewrite collapses both to int but must respect the SET semantics.
